mekki-muskil:180-180.t: His saying {وَلَا يَحسبن الَّذين يَبْخلُونَ}: whoever reads it with yāʾ (يَحسبن) makes الَّذين the fāʿil (agent) of حسب, and the first mafʿūl (object) is omitted because the context points to it; هو is a faṣl (separating pronoun), and خيرا is the second mafʿūl. Its implied form is: "And let not those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of His bounty think the miserliness to be good for them" (الْبُخْل خيرا لَهُم). يَبْخلُونَ points to "miserliness" (الْبُخْل), so its omission is permitted. As for whoever reads it with tāʾ (تحسبن) — and that is Ḥamza — he makes the one addressed the fāʿil, namely the Prophet, peace be upon him, and الَّذين is the first mafʿūl on the assumption that a muḍāf has been omitted and الَّذين put in its place; هو is a faṣl, and خيرا is the second mafʿūl. Its implied form is: "And do not think, O Muhammad, the miserliness of those who are miserly to be good for them" (وَلَا تحسبن يَا مُحَمَّد بخل الَّذين يَبْخلُونَ خيرا لَهُم). This implied element is indispensable so that the second mafʿūl is the same as the first in meaning. There is a point of objection in it, since it permits what is in the ṣila (relative clause) to explain what precedes the ṣila. Yet this reading has an advantage over the reading with yāʾ, because here you have omitted the mafʿūl but kept the muḍāf ilayhi standing in its place, whereas in the reading with yāʾ you omitted the mafʿūl and nothing remained to stand in its place. The reading with yāʾ also has an advantage over the reading with tāʾ: you omitted "miserliness" after يَبْخلُونَ had already come, whereas in the reading with tāʾ you omitted "miserliness" before يَبْخلُونَ comes, and made what is in the ṣila of الَّذين explain what precedes the ṣila. The two readings are equal in strength and weakness.

mekki-muskil:181-181.t: His saying {الَّذين قَالُوا إِن الله}: الَّذين is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal (substitute) for الَّذين in His saying لقد سمع الله قَول الَّذين; or in the position of the accusative on the implied verb أَعنِي ("I mean"); or in the position of the nominative on the implied هم ("they are").

mekki-muskil:183-183.t: His saying {أَلا نؤمن}: أَن is in the position of the accusative on the assumption that the preposition has been omitted, i.e. بِأَن لَا نؤمن ("that we should not believe"). أَن is written separate from لا if you assimilate it in speech with nasalization (ghunna); if you assimilate it without nasalization, you write it joined. This is the view of al-Mulhim, the companion of al-Akhfash. Others said: rather, it is written separate in every case. It has also been said: if you take أَن as lightened from the heavy (أنّ), you write it separate, because with it there is an implied pronoun that separates it, in intention, from what follows it; and if you take it as the أَن that puts the verb in the accusative, you write it joined, since there is no implied pronoun after it.

mekki-muskil:185-185.t: His saying {وَإِنَّمَا توفون أجوركم}: ما is the restraining (kāffa) mā that restrains إنّ from governing. It is not good to take ما in the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), because that would require أجوركم to be in the nominative, and no one read it so; for the implied form would then become "and indeed that which you are paid in full is your rewards" (وَإِن الَّذِي توفونه أجوركم), just as you say "indeed the one I honoured is ʿAmr" (أَن الَّذِي أكرمته عَمْرو). Moreover, you would be separating the ṣila from the relative noun by the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

mekki-muskil:188-188.t: His saying {لَا تحسبن الَّذين يفرحون}: whoever reads it with yāʾ makes the verb not transitive [here], and الَّذين يفرحون are the agents. Whoever reads فَلَا يحسبنهم with yāʾ makes it a badal (substitute) for لَا يَحسبن الَّذين يفرحون, according to the reading of whoever reads it with yāʾ; the fāʾ in فَلَا is redundant (zāʾida), so it does not prevent the badal. Since فَلَا يحسبنهم takes two objects, that dispenses with the need for وَلَا يَحسبن الَّذين يفرحون to take objects, because the second is a badal for it. So the proper course for whoever reads لَا يَحسبن الَّذين يفرحون with yāʾ is to read فَلَا يحسبنهم with yāʾ, so that it is a badal for the first and its taking objects makes the first's taking objects unnecessary. As for whoever reads the first with yāʾ and the second with tāʾ, the badal is not good there, because their agents differ; rather, the two objects of the first are omitted because the two objects of the second point to them. «[Translator's note: the source has «وَلكم يكون», evidently for «ولكن يكون» ("rather").]» As for whoever reads وَلَا يَحسبن الَّذين يفرحون with yāʾ — and they are the Kufans — they attributed the verb to the one addressed, namely the Prophet, peace be upon him. «[Translator's note: the source says "with yāʾ" here, but attributing the verb to the one addressed requires the reading with tāʾ (تحسبن), which is the Kufan reading; translated as written.]» الَّذين يفرحون is the first mafʿūl (object) of حسب, and the second is omitted because what follows it points to it, namely بمفازة من الْعَذَاب. It has also been said that بمفازة من الْعَذَاب is the second mafʿūl of the first حسب on the assumption of fronting, so the second mafʿūl of the second حسب is omitted because the first points to it. Its implied form is: "Do not think, O Muhammad, those who rejoice in what they have been given to be in safety from the punishment; do not think them to be in safety from the punishment" (لَا تحسبن يَا مُحَمَّد الَّذين يفرحون بِمَا أُوتُوا بمفازة من الْعَذَاب فَلَا تحسبنهم بمفازة من الْعَذَاب); then the second was omitted, just as you say "I thought Zayd to be going, and I thought ʿAmr" (ظَنَنْت زيدا ذَاهِبًا وظننت عمرا), meaning "going" (ذَاهِبًا), and you omit it because the first points to it. «[Translator's note: the source has a stray numeral «٢» before ذَاهِبًا.]» It is also possible for تحسبنهم, in the reading of whoever reads with tāʾ, to be a badal for تحسبن الَّذين يفرحون in the reading of whoever also reads with tāʾ, since the agents and objects agree; the fāʾ is redundant and does not prevent the badal. As for whoever reads the first with tāʾ and the second with yāʾ, the badal is not good in the second because their agents differ; rather, the second mafʿūl of the first حسب is omitted because what follows it points to it, or بمفازة من الْعَذَاب is its second mafʿūl and the second mafʿūl of the second حسب is omitted, as we mentioned at first.

mekki-muskil:191-191.t:
His saying {الَّذين يذكرُونَ الله}: الَّذين is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal (substitute) for أولي; or in the position of the accusative on أَعنِي ("I mean"); or in the position of the nominative on هم الَّذين ("they are those who"). The singular of أولي is ذِي, the one used as a muḍāf. If it is accusative, as in يَا أولي الْأَلْبَاب, its singular is ذَا used as a muḍāf; and if it is nominative, as in أولُوا بَقِيَّة, its singular is ذُو used as a muḍāf. We have already mentioned that the singular of أُولَئِكَ is the vague (mubham) ذَا, from your saying هَذَا.
His saying {قيَاما وقعودا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent pronoun in يذكرُونَ. His saying وعَلى جنُوبهم is also a ḥāl from it, in the position of the accusative, as though He said "and lying on their sides" (ومضطجعين). His saying ويتفكرون is conjoined to يذكرُونَ, included in the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذين.
His saying {بَاطِلا}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for falsehood" (للباطل).
His saying {سُبْحَانَكَ}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the place of تسبيحا, i.e. "we glorify You with glorification" (نسبحك تسبيحا); its meaning is: we declare You exalted far above evil and declare You free of it.

mekki-muskil:193-193.t:
His saying {أَن آمنُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative on the omission of the preposition, i.e. بِأَن آمنُوا ("saying: Believe").
His saying {وتوفنا مَعَ الْأَبْرَار}: i.e. "take us as righteous ones along with the righteous" (توفنا ابرارا مَعَ الْأَبْرَار), as the poet said:
... كَأَنَّك من جمال بني أقيش ... يقعقع خلف رجلَيْهِ بشن ...
(As though you were one of the camels of Banū Uqaysh, with a dry water-skin rattled behind his legs.)
i.e. "as though you were a camel from the camels of Banū Uqaysh" (كَأَنَّك جمل من جمال بني أقيش). The singular of الْأَبْرَار is بار, and it may be that its singular is برّ, originally برر, like كتف.

mekki-muskil:195-195.t:
His saying {أَنِّي لَا أضيع عمل}: أَن is in the position of the accusative, i.e. بِأَنِّي ("that I…"). Ibn ʿUmar read إِنِّي with kasra, on the implied form "so He said: Indeed I do not let be lost" (فَقَالَ إِنِّي لَا أضيع).
His saying {ثَوابًا من عِنْد الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the Basrans, so it is an emphatic maṣdar. Al-Kisāʾī said it is accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment), i.e. as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said it is accusative as tafsīr (specification).
His saying {وَالله عِنْده حسن الثَّوَاب}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), حسن is a second mubtadaʾ, عِنْده is the khabar (predicate) of حسن, and حسن with its khabar is the khabar of the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
His saying {فَالَّذِينَ هَاجرُوا}: a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is لأكفرن.

mekki-muskil:197-197.t: His saying {مَتَاع قَلِيل}: it is nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is an enjoyment" (هُوَ مَتَاع) or "that is an enjoyment" (ذَلِك مَتَاع), and the like.

mekki-muskil:198-198.t:
His saying {تجْرِي من تحتهَا الْأَنْهَار}: in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات; or, if you wish, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative latent pronoun in لَهُم — since it is like a verb coming after its agent — if you make جنَّات nominative as a mubtadaʾ. If you make it nominative by the [implied verb of] being-established (al-istiqrār), there is no nominative pronoun in لَهُم, since it is then like a verb preceding its agent; so understand it.
His saying {خَالِدين فِيهَا}: a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in لَهُم. That which governs the ḥāl and puts it in the accusative is always that which governs the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), because it is the same as it.
His saying {نزلا}: what is said about it, and the disagreement, is like ثَوابًا.

mekki-muskil:199-199.t: His saying {خاشعين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يُؤمن or in إِلَيْهِم. Likewise لَا يشْتَرونَ is like خاشعين.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, {الم}: like الم ذَلِك [Translator's note: the source reads «لم ذَلِك»; the reference is to the opening of al-Baqara]. As for the fatḥa of the mīm, it may have been given fatḥa because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām after it; it may have been given fatḥa because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the yāʾ before it, with no pause intended on it; and it may have been given fatḥa because a pause was intended on it, so the vowel of the connecting alif with which (the next word) begins was thrown onto it, as they said "one, two, three, four (وَاحِد اثْنَان ثَلَاثَة أَرْبَعَة)": they threw the vowel of the hamza of أَرْبَعَة onto the hāʾ of ثَلَاثَة and left it as it was, and did not change it to tāʾ when vowelling it, since the intention in it is the pause. Ibn Kaysān said that the alif of الله, and every alif with the lām of definiteness, is a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ), like قد, and it was made connective only because of frequent use; so whoever vowels the mīm throws onto it the vowel of the hamza, which is like the qāf of قد, in الله, and so gives it fatḥa with the fatḥa of the hamza. Al-Akhfash allowed kasra on the mīm because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and that is a mistake with no analogy to support it, because of its heaviness.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying {الله لَا إِلَه إِلَّا هُوَ}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is نزل عَلَيْك الْكتاب. As for لا إله إلا هو: لا إله is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar is omitted, and إلا هو is a badal (substitute) from the position of لا إله. It was said it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الله; and it was said from the pronoun in نزل, its implied form being "Allah sent down the Book upon you, being alone in lordship". And it was said هو is a badal from the position of لا إله.
His saying بِالْحَقِّ: in the position of a ḥāl from الْكتاب, so the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being "He sent down upon you the Book, established with the truth". The bāʾ is not attached to نزل, because it has already passed to two objects, one of them by a particle, so it does not pass to a third. Likewise مُصدقا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in بِالْحَقِّ, its implied form being "He sent down upon you the Book, verified, confirming what was before it"; and they are two emphatic ḥāls (ḥāl muʾakkida).
His saying {الْحَيّ القيوم}: two naʿts (adjectives) of الله; القيوم is of the pattern فيعول from قَامَ بِالْأَمر (he undertook the matter), and it has been mentioned.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {التَّوْرَاة}: its pattern is فوعلة and its origin is وورية, derived from وري الزند (the fire-stick gave out fire); the tāʾ is a replacement of wāw. From وري الزند are His saying تورون and His saying فالموريات قدحا. The yāʾ was turned into alif because it was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa. This is the doctrine of the Basrans. The Kufans said its pattern is تفعلة, also from وري الزند, and the tāʾ according to them is not changed from wāw, its origin being تورية. This (pattern) is rare in the language while فوعلة is common in the language, so taking it according to the more common is more fitting. Also, the addition of tāʾ at the beginning of a word is not frequent, as the addition of wāw as the second letter is frequent.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {ابْتِغَاء الْفِتْنَة وابتغاء تَأْوِيله}: two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose).
His saying {والراسخون فِي الْعلم}: conjoined to الله, exalted be His mention; so they know the ambiguous (al-mutashābih), and for that reason Allah the Exalted described them as firmly grounded in knowledge; had they been ignorant of the knowledge of the ambiguous, they would not have been described as firmly grounded in knowledge. As for what is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read وَيَقُول الراسخون فِي الْعلم آمنا بِهِ, it is a reading that differs from the muṣḥaf; and if it is authentic, its interpretation is "none knows it but Allah and those firmly grounded in knowledge, and they say: we believe in it"; then the pronoun in يَقُولُونَ was made overt, and he said وَيَقُول الراسخون. We have devoted a separate book to this question because of the breadth of discussion on it. The hāʾ in تَأْوِيله refers back to the ambiguous; and it was said it refers back to the Book, which is the whole Quran.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {كدأب آل فِرْعَوْن}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form according to al-Farrāʾ being "the Arabs disbelieved with a disbelief like the disbelief of the family of Pharaoh". In this view there is a suggestion of separation between the ṣila (relative clause) and the relative noun.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying {فِئَة}: i.e. "one of them is a party".
His saying {تقَاتل}: in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of فئة. If you put فِئَة in the genitive as a badal (substitute) from فئتين, it would be permissible, and that is the reading of al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid; أُخْرَى would then be in the position of the genitive.
His saying {وَأُخْرَى}: in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is an adjective standing in place of the described noun, namely فِئَة; its implied form is "and the other is another, disbelieving party". The accusative in both is also permissible as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they met, being different".
His saying {ترونهم}: whoever reads it with tāʾ, its position is accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm in لكم; or in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of أخرى; or in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of أخرى, if you put it (أخرى) in the position of the genitive by conjunction with فِئَة in the reading of whoever puts it in the genitive as a badal from فئتين. The address in لكم is to the Jews; and it was said to the Muslims. In this verse there are aspects of i'rab and meanings according to the disagreement about what the pronouns in His saying ترونهم مثليهم refer to, and according to the difference of meanings in the reading of whoever reads ترونهم with yāʾ; mentioning them would be long, and we have composed a separate book to explain them.
His saying {مثليهم}: accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in ترونهم, because it is from seeing with the eye, as shown by His saying رَأْي الْعين. The accusative pronoun in ترونهم refers back to the other, disbelieving party; the nominative one, in the reading of whoever reads with tāʾ, refers back to the kāf and mīm in لكم, and in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ it refers back to the party fighting in the way of Allah; and the hāʾ and mīm in مثليهم refer back to the party fighting in the way of Allah. This is the clearest of the views, and there is much disagreement about it.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {وَالله عِنْده حسن المآب}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), حسن is a second mubtadaʾ, عنده is the khabar (predicate) of حسن, and حسن with its khabar is the khabar about the name الله. ولمآب [Translator's note: so in the source, for «والمآب»]: its pattern is مفعل and its origin is مأوب; then the vowel of the wāw was shifted onto the hamza and the wāw was replaced by alif, like مقَال and مَكَان.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying {جنَّات}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and للذين is the khabar (predicate); the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar in whose place the lām stands, like your saying لله الْحَمد. The genitive in جنَّات is permissible as a badal (substitute) from بِخَير, on the basis that you make the lām in الَّذين attached to أنبئكم, or make it a description of خير. If you made the lām attached to something omitted in whose place it stands, the genitive of جنَّات would not be permissible, because when prepositions and ẓarfs (adverbs) are attached to something omitted in whose place they stand, an implied (muqaddar) nominative pronoun comes to be in them, and they need a mubtadaʾ to which that pronoun refers back, as in your saying "Zayd has wealth (لزيد مَال)", "in the house is Zayd (فِي الدَّار زيد)" and "behind you is ʿAmr (خلفك عَمْرو)"; so جنَّات must be nominative when the lām is attached to something omitted. If you supposed the lām attached to something omitted with no pronoun in it, you would put جنَّات in the nominative by its verb (as fāʿil, agent), and that is the doctrine of al-Akhfash in putting what follows ẓarfs and genitive-governing particles in the nominative by the (implied verb of) settling (al-istiqrār). The skilled grammarians consider that good only when the ẓarfs or genitive-governing particles are a description of what precedes them; then the nominative of the noun by the istiqrār becomes well-established and good. We have explained it more clearly than this in other places in this book and illustrated it with examples. Likewise if they are ḥāls (circumstantials) of what precedes them.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {الَّذين يَقُولُونَ}: الَّذين is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from للَّذين اتَّقوا; or, if you wish, in the position of the nominative on (an implied) هم; or, if you wish, in the position of the accusative as praise (madḥ).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: And His saying {الصابرين}: a badal (substitute) from الَّذين, according to the different aspects mentioned.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {قَائِما بِالْقِسْطِ}: an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial) from هُوَ.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {إِن الدّين عِنْد الله الْإِسْلَام}: whoever reads أن with fatḥa, which is the reading of al-Kisāʾī, makes it a badal (substitute) from the first أَن in His saying شهد الله أَنه; it is the badal of a thing from a thing when it is the same thing. The badal may also be a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), on the supposition of the second including the first, because al-islām includes many laws, among them the tawḥīd mentioned before; it is like your saying "Zayd was robbed of his garment (سلب زيد ثَوْبه)". It is also permissible for أَن to be in the position of the genitive as a badal from الْقسْط, a badal of a thing from a thing when it is the same thing.
His saying {بغيا بَينهم}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and it was said a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذين.
His saying {وَمن يكفر بآيَات الله}: من is conditional, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
And His saying {فَإِن الله سريع الْحساب}: its khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, and the pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ from its khabar is omitted, its implied form being "swift in reckoning for him". The nominative of يكفر is also permissible, making من in the sense of الَّذين and implying the omission of لَهُم from the khabar.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {وَمن اتبعن}: من is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the tāʾ in أسلمت. It is also permissible for it to be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "and whoever follows me has submitted his face to Allah". It is also permissible for it to be in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الله.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {فبشرهم بِعَذَاب}: the khabar (predicate) of إِن الَّذين يكفرون. The fāʾ entered because of the vagueness in الَّذين, together with the verb being in the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذين, and together with no governing word having changed the meaning of الَّذين. The entry of the fāʾ into the khabar of الَّذِي is not complete until the verb is in its ṣila and no governing word that changes its meaning has entered upon it; with these two conditions the fāʾ enters the khabar of الَّذِي, and whenever both or one of them is lacking, the entry of the fāʾ into its khabar is not permissible. This has been mentioned before.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {وهم معرضون}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of فريق, or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the indefinite noun has been described and because the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying {فَكيف إِذا جمعناهم}: كَيفَ is a question about a state, and here it is a threat and warning. Its position is accusative as a ẓarf (adverb), and what governs it is the meaning that كَيفَ indicates; its implied form is "then in what state will they be when they are gathered for a day about which there is no doubt?". What governs إِذا is what كَيفَ indicates. There is latitude in ẓarfs: the meanings indicated by the discourse govern them, unlike objects. This is a principle that recurs frequently in the Quran and in speech.
His saying {لَا ريب فِيهِ}: in the position of the genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of يَوْم.
His saying {وهم لَا يظْلمُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in كسبت.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His saying {مَالك الْملك}: accusative as an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf). According to Sībawayh it is not permissible for it to be a naʿt (adjective) of His saying اللَّهُمَّ; according to him اللَّهُمَّ is not described, because it has been altered by what is at its end. Others among the Basrans and the Kufans allowed مَالك الْملك to be a description of اللَّهُمَّ, as it is permissible with «بِاللَّه» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «يا الله»].
His saying {تؤتي الْملك من تشَاء}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مَالك; and likewise وتنزع الْملك مِمَّن تشَاء, and likewise وتعز and وتذل. It is also permissible for all of this to be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "You give dominion and take away dominion". His saying بِيَدِك الْخَيْر: a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in مَالك; and it is permissible for the sentence to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "You: in Your hand is good".

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying {تولج اللَّيْل فِي النَّهَار وتولج النَّهَار فِي اللَّيْل}: like تؤتي الْملك من تشَاء in its two aspects [Translator's note: i.e. a ḥāl (circumstantial) or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ]; and likewise وَتخرج and وترزق.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {تقاة}: its pattern is فعلة and its origin is وقية; then they replaced the wāw with tāʾ, as in تجاه and تكأة, and it became تقية; then the yāʾ was turned into alif because it was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa, and it became تقاة.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t:
His saying {يَوْم تَجِد كل نفس}: يَوْم is accusative by يحذركم, i.e. "and Allah warns you of Himself on the day you find", and there is room for reflection in this. It is also permissible for what governs it to be an implied verb, i.e. "remember, O Muhammad, the day you find". It is also permissible for what governs it to be الْمصير, i.e. "and to Him is the return on the day you find". And it is permissible for what governs it to be قَدِيرًا, i.e. "able on the day you find".
His saying {محضرا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun omitted from the ṣila (relative clause) of مَا, its implied form being "what it did of good, made present".
His saying {وَمَا عملت من سوء}: مَا is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the first مَا, and تود is a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in the second عملت. If you cut it off from what precedes it and make it conditional, you put تود in the jussive, making it the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition and the khabar (predicate) of مَا. It is also permissible to cut it off from the first, on the basis that it is in the sense of الَّذِي, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with تود as the khabar.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {ذُرِّيَّة}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nouns before it, in the sense of "related, some of them from others". And it was said it is a badal (substitute) from what precedes it.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {إِذْ قَالَت}: what governs إِذْ is سميع عليم, i.e. "and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing when she said". It was said what governs it is اصْطفى, i.e. "and He chose the family of ʿImrān when she said", and there is room for reflection in this. It was said what governs it is implied, its implied form being "and remember, O Muhammad, when she said"; on this implied form it is good to begin (reading) with it, and it is not good on the other (views).
His saying {محررا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَا; and it was said its implied form is "a boy dedicated", i.e. devoted purely to You. مَا is used here for a rational being because of vagueness, as the Arabs said "take from my slaves what (مَا) you wish", and Sībawayh reported "glory be to what (مَا) the thunder glorifies with His praise", and as Allah the Exalted said فأنكحوا مَا طَابَ لكم من النِّسَاء. The hāʾ in وَضَعتهَا refers back to مَا, and its meaning is feminine.

mekki-muskil:36-36.t:
His saying {وَضَعتهَا أُنْثَى}: أُنْثَى is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun in وَضَعتهَا; and it is permissible for it to be a badal (substitute) from it.
His saying {وَالله أعلم بِمَا وضعت}: whoever gives ḍamma to the tāʾ and makes the ʿayn quiescent (وضعْتُ) does not begin (a new reading) with His saying وَالله أعلم بِمَا وضعت, because it is part of the speech of Maryam's mother; whoever gives fatḥa to the ʿayn and makes the tāʾ quiescent (وضعَتْ) begins with it, because it is not part of the speech of Maryam's mother. Similar is whoever gives kasra to the tāʾ and makes the ʿayn quiescent (وضعْتِ), which is a reading reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t:
His saying / زَكَرِيَّاء /: the hamza of زَكَرِيَّاء is for the feminine. It cannot be for ilḥāq (assimilation to a pattern), because there is no pattern on its measure among the basic forms to which it could be assimilated. Nor can it be changed (from another letter), because the change cannot but be from a letter of the word itself or from a letter of ilḥāq; it cannot be from the word itself, because yāʾ and wāw are not radical in what is of four letters; and it cannot be from a letter of ilḥāq, since there is no form among the basic patterns to which this could be assimilated. So the hamza can only be for the feminine. Likewise is the analysis according to the reading of whoever shortens it (زكريا): the alif is for the feminine, by these proofs.
His saying {كلما دخل}: كلما is a ẓarf (adverb) of time, and what governs it is وجد, i.e. "whatever time he entered upon her, he found provision with her".

mekki-muskil:38-38.t:
His saying {هُنَالك}: a ẓarf (adverb) of time, and what governs it is دَعَا, i.e. "Zakariyyā called upon his Lord at that time". هُنَالك may be, in another place, an adverb of place, which is its origin; it was only extended in use and so came to be used for time by the indication of the situation and the discourse. Sometimes it admits both aspects together, as in His saying هُنَالك الْولَايَة لله. What shows that its origin is place is that you say "sit there (اجْلِسْ هُنَالك)" meaning the place, whereas "travel there (سر هُنَالك)" meaning the time is not permissible. The ẓarf is هُنَا, the lām is for emphasis, and the kāf is for address, having no position in i'rab.
His saying {ذُرِّيَّة}: its pattern is فعولة from ذَرأ الله الْخلق (Allah created creation); its origin on this (view) was ذروءة; they replaced the hamza with yāʾ, so a yāʾ and a wāw came together with the first quiescent, and they assimilated the yāʾ into the wāw, with the second assimilated to the first [Translator's note: so in the source], out of finding the wāws heavy; and the rāʾ was given kasra so that the quiescent assimilated yāʾ would be sound. It was said that ذُرِّيَّة is فعيلة from الذَّر (tiny ants), so the origin of الذُّرِّيَّة was a name for a man's small children, and then it was extended; its origin on this (view) was ذريرة; then they replaced the last rāʾ with yāʾ and the first was assimilated into it, because of the coming together of the rāʾs, as they said تظنيت for تظننت because of the coming together of the nūns. It was said the pattern of ذُرِّيَّة is فعولة from ذروت, so its origin on this (view) is ذرورة; then the same was done with it as in the preceding aspect before this one, and the doubled rāʾ was given kasra so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t:
His saying {وَهُوَ قَائِم يُصَلِّي}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in فنادته; and يُصَلِّي is in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in قَائِم.
His saying {مُصدقا}: a ḥāl from يحيى, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara); and likewise وَسَيِّدًا, وَحَصُورًا and وَنَبِيًّا.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t:
His saying {عَاقِر}: it came without hāʾ only by way of attribution (nisba); had it come according to the verb, He would have said عقيرة, in the sense of معقورة, i.e. she has a barrenness that prevents her from (having) a child.
His saying {كَذَلِك الله يفعل}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "Allah does what He wills, a doing like that".

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying {اجْعَل لي آيَة}: اجْعَل is in the sense of صير (make), so it passes to two objects, one of them by a particle; they are لي and آيَة.
His saying {أَلا تكلم النَّاس}: أَن لَا is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of آيتك. The nominative of تكلم is also permissible, on the basis that you imply the kāf with أَن, i.e. "your sign is that you (أَنَّك) will not speak to people". And ثَلَاثَة is a ẓarf (adverb).
His saying {إِلَّا رمزا}: an exception not of the first kind; and every exception not of the genus of the first, the right way in it is the accusative.
His saying {كثيرا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "much remembrance".

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying {وَإِذ قَالَت الْمَلَائِكَة}: إِذْ is conjoined to إِذْ قَالَت امْرَأَة عمرَان, when you make it in the position of the accusative by (an implied) "remember".

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {أَيهمْ يكفل مَرْيَم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the sentence is in the position of the accusative by a verb indicated by the speech; its implied form is "when they cast their pens, looking (to see) which of them would take charge of Maryam". (The verb) does not govern the wording of أي, because it is an interrogative, and what precedes an interrogative does not govern it.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t:
His saying {إِذْ قَالَت الْمَلَائِكَة}: what governs إِذْ is يختصمون, i.e. "they were disputing when the angels said". It is also permissible for the second وَمَا كنت لديهم to govern it, as the first governed إِذْ يلقون.
His saying {وجيها}, His saying وَمن المقربين, His saying ويكلم النَّاس فِي المهد, His saying وكهلا, His saying وَمن الصَّالِحين: all of that is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عِيسَى; and likewise His saying ويعلمه and His saying ورسولا. It was said (of ورسولا) that its implied form is "and We make him a messenger", so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and it was said it is a ḥāl, its implied form being "and he speaks to them as a messenger". Whoever makes الْكَلِمَة in His saying بِكَلِمَة مِنْهُ a name for ʿĪsā, then according to his view وجيه in the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of كلمة, would be permissible outside the Quran. (…) in the position of the accusative on the implied omission of the genitive-governing particle, its implied form being "with (بِ) that I have come to you" [Translator's note: the text appears to have a gap here; this part evidently concerns أَنِّي قد جِئتُكُمْ in verse 49]. Whoever reads إني with kasra does so as cut off (qaṭʿ) and beginning anew. It is also permissible that whoever reads أَنِّي أخلق with fatḥa makes it a badal (substitute) from آيَة, so that أَن is in the position of the genitive; and it is permissible for أَن to be in the position of the nominative on the implied omission of a mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is that I create".

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying {كَهَيئَةِ الطير فأنفخ فِيهِ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a creating like the shape of a bird". The hāʾ in فِيهِ refers back to the thing shaped, because the blowing was only into the thing shaped, which is the form; whereas الهيئة is only the maṣdar, the noun of the action, and there is no blowing into it; but the maṣdar has taken the place of the object, as one says "this is the creation (خلق) of Allah", i.e. what is created by Him, and "this is a dirham of the minting (ضرب) of the emir", i.e. minted by him. It may also be that the hāʾ refers back to the created thing, because أخلق indicates it, since it indicates creating by virtue of being derived from it, and creating indicates the created thing. And it is permissible for the hāʾ to refer back to the kāf in كَهَيئَةِ, since it is in the sense of مثل (likeness).

mekki-muskil:50-50.t: His saying {ومصدقا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ in جِئتُكُمْ, i.e. "I have come to you confirming". It is not good to conjoin ومصدقا to وجيها, because then the wording would have to be "what was before him (لما بَين يَدَيْهِ)", whereas the recitation is "what was before me (لما بَين يَدي)".

mekki-muskil:55-55.t:
His saying {إِذْ قَالَ الله يَا عِيسَى}: إِذْ is in the position of the accusative by an implied "remember (اذكر)".
His saying {وجاعل الَّذين اتبعوك}: جَاعل is not conjoined to what precedes it, because it is an address to the Prophet ﷺ while the first is to ʿĪsā. And it was said it is conjoined to the first, and both are to ʿĪsā, upon him be peace.

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {الْحق من رَبك}: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the truth" or "this is the truth".

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His saying {وَمَا من إِلَه إِلَّا الله}: إله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and إِلَّا الله is its khabar (predicate), as you say "there is no one but is thankful to you (مَا من أحد إِلَّا شاكرك)": أحد is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, من is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and إلا شاكرك is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. It is also permissible for the khabar of the mubtadaʾ to be omitted, with إِلَّا الله a badal (substitute) from إله according to the position; its implied form is "there is no god worshipped", or "existing", "except Allah".

mekki-muskil:64-64.t:
His saying {إِلَى كلمة سَوَاء}: سَوَاء is a naʿt (adjective) of كلمة. Al-Ḥasan read سَوَاءً in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it is in the place of اسْتِوَاء, i.e. "it was equal, an equality".
His saying {أَلا نعْبد}: أَن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from كلمة; or, if you wish, in the position of the nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is that we worship not". It is also permissible for it to be in the sense of أي, explicative (mufassira), on the basis that you put نعْبد and نشرك in the jussive by لا. If you made it lightened from the heavy (أنّ), you would put نعْبد and نشْرك in the nominative and imply the hāʾ (pronoun) with أَن.

mekki-muskil:68-68.t: His saying {وَهَذَا النَّبِي}: you put النَّبِي in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of هَذَا, or as a badal (substitute), or as an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); and هَذَا is in the position of the nominative by conjunction with الَّذين. If وَهَذَا النَّبِيَّ were said in the accusative in ordinary speech, it would be good to conjoin it to the hāʾ in اتَّبعُوهُ.

mekki-muskil:73-73.t:
His saying {وَلَا تؤمنوا إِلَّا لمن تبع دينكُمْ}, then He said أَن يُؤْتى أحد مثل مَا: أَن is an object of تؤمنوا, and the implied form of the speech is "and do not believe that anyone is given the like of what you were given except whoever follows your religion"; on this (view) the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and من is in the position of the accusative, an exception not of the first kind. It was said [Translator's note: the source reads «وقيا», evidently «وقيل»] the implied form is "and do not believe, except whoever follows your religion, that anyone is given". Al-Farrāʾ said the speech is cut off at His saying دينكُمْ; then He said to Muhammad, upon him be peace: "Say: the guidance is the guidance of Allah — that anyone should be given the like of what you were given", so لا is implied.
It is also permissible for the lām to be non-redundant and attached to what the speech indicates, because the meaning of the speech is "do not acknowledge that anyone is given the like of what you were given except to (لِ) whoever follows your religion"; so both particles are attached to تقروا, as you say "I acknowledged to Zayd a thousand (أَقرَرت لزيد بِأَلف)". That is permissible because the first is like a ẓarf (adverb), so it becomes like your saying "I passed in the market by Zayd (مَرَرْت فِي السُّوق بزيد)". أحد entered only because the wording of negation precedes it in His saying وَلَا تؤمنوا; it is a prohibition and its wording is the wording of negation.
As for whoever lengthens it and makes it a question (آن يُؤْتى), which is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, he brought it in the sense of the Jews' denial that anyone should be given the like of what they were given, reporting their words. So it is permissible for أَن to be in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), since what precedes does not govern أَن because of the interrogative, and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being "that anyone is given the like of what you were given — do you believe it?", or "do you acknowledge it?", and the like. Beginning with أن is good because it rests upon the interrogative particle, so in illustration it is like أَزِيد ضَربته. It is also permissible for أَن to be in the position of the accusative, and that is the preferred choice, as in your saying أزيدا ضَربته the accusative is the preferred choice, because the question is about the action; so you imply a verb between the alif and أَن, its implied form being "do you broadcast that anyone is given the like of what you were given?", "do you spread…?", "do you mention…?" and the like, of what is indicated by the denial they intended with the wording of the interrogative. What shows that they intended this meaning is His saying, Exalted is He, reporting what they said to their companions: أتحدثونهم بِمَا فتح الله عَلَيْكُم, meaning: do you tell the Muslims what you found of the description of their Prophet in your Book, ليحاجوكم بِهِ عِنْد ربكُم.
أحد in the reading of whoever lengthens is in the sense of واحد (one). He used the plural in His saying ليحاجوكم only because He referred it back to the meaning of أحد, since it has the sense of multitude; but أحد, when it is in negation, is stronger in indicating multitude than when it is in affirmation. The entry of أحد after the wording of the interrogative is good because it is in the sense of denial and negation, so أحد entered after it as it enters after an explicitly pronounced negation; on this (view) it may be in its original sense of generality and not in the sense of واحد.

mekki-muskil:75-75.t:
His saying {دمت}: whoever gives ḍamma to the dāl makes it فعل يفعل, like قَالَ يَقُول and دام يَدُوم; and whoever gives kasra to the dāl makes it فعل يفعل, like خَافَ يخَاف, on دَامَ يدام [Translator's note: the source does not mark the vowels of the two patterns, i.e. faʿala yafʿulu and faʿila yafʿalu]. Likewise مت, for whoever gives kasra or ḍamma to the mīm.
Ḥumayd read يلون with a single wāw and ḍamma on the lām. The origin of this reading is يلوون; then the first wāw was given hamza because of its ḍamma, then the vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the lām, according to the principle of lightening used in the speech of the Arabs.

mekki-muskil:80-80.t: His saying {وَلَا يَأْمُركُمْ أَن تَتَّخِذُوا}: whoever reads يَأْمُركُمْ in the accusative conjoins it to أَن يؤتيه الله or to ثمَّ يَقُول, and the pronoun in يَأْمُركُمْ is for the human being (البشر). Whoever reads it in the nominative cuts it off from what precedes it and makes لَا in the sense of لَيْسَ, and the pronoun in يَأْمُركُمْ is for Allah, exalted be His mention.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t:
His saying {لما آتيتكم من كتاب وَحِكْمَة}: whoever gives kasra to the lām, namely Ḥamza, attaches it to the taking, i.e. Allah took the covenant because of what they were given of the Book and wisdom, since whoever is given that is the most excellent, and the covenant is taken from him; and مَا is in the sense of الَّذِي.
As for whoever gives fatḥa to the lām, it is the lām of ibtidāʾ (the lām of the subject), and it is a response to what is indicated of the meaning of an oath, because the taking of a covenant is only by oaths and pledges; so the lām is the response to the oath, and مَا is in the sense of الَّذِي, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the hāʾ is omitted from آتيتكم, its implied form being "that which I gave you (آتيتكموه) of a Book"; and the khabar (predicate) is من كتاب وَحِكْمَة, with من redundant (zāʾida). It was said the khabar is لتؤمنن بِهِ, which is the response to an omitted oath, its implied form being "by Allah, you shall surely believe in him". The returning pronoun from the sentence conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) is taken according to the meaning according to al-Akhfash, because لما مَعكُمْ means "to what I gave you (آتيتموه) [Translator's note: so in the source] of the Book", just as He said إِنَّه من يتق ويصبر فَإِن الله لَا يضيع أجر الْمُحْسِنِينَ, taking the pronoun according to the meaning, since it is in the sense of "Allah does not let their reward be lost". This returning pronoun must be implied in the sentence conjoined to the ṣila, which is ثمَّ جَاءَكُم رَسُول مُصدق لما مَعكُمْ; they are two sentences for two relative nouns, the second of which was dropped for brevity and the conjunction stood in its place, so there must be in both ṣilas a returning pronoun to both relative nouns. Do you not see that if you said الَّذِي قَامَ أَبوهُ ثمَّ زيد منطلق عَمْرو it would not be permissible until you say "to him (إِلَيْهِ)" or "for his sake (من أَجله)" ʿAmr, and the like, so that in the conjoined sentence there is something referring back to الَّذِي, which is the omitted one, as there was in the sentence that is the ṣila of الَّذِي; then you bring the khabar of the mubtadaʾ after that. It is possible that the returning pronoun from the second ṣila is omitted, its implied form being "then there comes to you a messenger with it (بِهِ)", i.e. with confirming it, i.e. with confirming what I gave you. This omission is by analogy with what al-Khalīl allowed of your saying مَا أَنا بِالَّذِي قَائِل لَك شَيْئا, i.e. "by the one who is (هُوَ) saying", and as was read تَمامًا على الَّذِي احسنُ in the nominative, i.e. "who is (هُوَ) best"; then the pronoun was dropped from the ṣila. This omission is considered far-fetched by the Basrans only because the pronoun is attached to a preposition, so what is omitted from the speech is a pronoun and a particle; that is why it is far-fetched.
It is also permissible, in the reading of whoever gives fatḥa to the lām, for مَا to be conditional, so that it is in the position of the accusative by آتيتكم, and جَاءَكُم is conjoined to it, also in the position of the jussive. The lām in لما would then be a lām of emphasis and not the response to the oath as it was in the first aspect; rather it entered to receive the oath, like the lām in لَئِن لم ينْتَه المُنَافِقُونَ: it gives warning of the coming of the oath after it, namely His saying لتؤمنن بِهِ, just as لَئِن was a warning of the oath in His saying لنغرينك. So it is a preparation (tawṭiʾa) for the oath and not the response to the oath as it was in the first aspect, because the condition is not attached to what precedes it and what precedes it does not govern it, so it became cut off from what precedes it — unlike when you make مَا in the sense of الَّذِي, because then it is speech connected to what precedes it and a response to it. Dropping it (the lām) is permissible; Allah the Exalted said وان لم ينْتَهوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ ليمسن. When مَا is conditional, the conjoined sentence does not need a returning pronoun, just as the first did not need it. For that reason al-Khalīl and Sībawayh chose it: since they did not see a returning pronoun in the second sentence, they made مَا conditional. This is the explanation by al-Māzinī and others of the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; and some have interpreted Sībawayh's doctrine as being that مَا is in the sense of الَّذِي.
The hāʾ in بِهِ refers back to مَا when it is in the sense of الَّذِي, and it is not permissible for it to refer back to رَسُول. The hāʾ in لتنصرنه refers back to رَسُول in both aspects. This is a verse of unusual i'rab, so understand it.

mekki-muskil:83-83.t: His saying {طَوْعًا وَكرها}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "willing and compelled".

mekki-muskil:84-84.t: His saying {قل آمنا بِاللَّه}: i.e. "say: say 'we believe'"; so the pronoun in آمنا is for those commanded, and the one commanding them is the Prophet ﷺ. It is also permissible for the command to be to the Prophet ﷺ with his community being meant by it.

mekki-muskil:85-85.t:
His saying {دينا}: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)), and غير is the object of يبتغي. It is also permissible for غير to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) and دينا the object of يَبْتَغِي.
His saying {وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَة من الخاسرين}: the ẓarf (adverbial phrase) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the speech indicates, i.e. "and he is a loser in the Hereafter, among the losers". It is not good to attach it to الخاسرين, because of the ṣila (relative clause) preceding the relative noun, unless you make the alif and lām for definiteness and not in the sense of الَّذِي; then it is good.

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {أَن عَلَيْهِم لعنة الله}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of جزاؤهم, and جزاؤهم with its khabar is the khabar of أُولَئِكَ. It is also permissible for جزاؤهم to be a badal (substitute) from أُولَئِكَ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), with أَن the khabar of جزاؤهم.

mekki-muskil:88-88.t:
His saying {خَالِدين فِيهَا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in عَلَيْهِم.
His saying {لَا يُخَفف عَنْهُم}: like it; and it is permissible for it to be cut off from the first.

mekki-muskil:91-91.t:
His saying {وماتوا وهم كفار}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مَاتُوا.
His saying {وَمَا لَهُم من ناصرين}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar; مَا is negating and من is redundant (zāʾida), and the sentence is in the position of a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in the first لَهُم.

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His saying {مُبَارَكًا وَهدى}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun, in the position of the accusative [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the pronoun in وُضِعَ]. The nominative is permissible, on "it is blessed (هُوَ مبارك)", and the genitive is permissible as a naʿt (adjective) of بيت.

mekki-muskil:97-97.t:
His saying {مقَام إِبْرَاهِيم}: i.e. "among the signs is the station of Ibrāhīm", so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted. It is also permissible for مقَام to be a badal (substitute) from الْآيَات, on the basis that the station of Ibrāhīm is the whole sanctuary (al-ḥaram), in which there are many signs; that is the view of Mujāhid, and his proof is وَمن دخله كَانَ آمنا, meaning the sanctuary without disagreement. It was said it is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the station of Ibrāhīm".
His saying {وَمن دخله كَانَ آمنا}: من is conjoined to مقَام according to its (various) aspects; and it is permissible for it to be a mubtadaʾ beginning anew, cut off, with كَانَ آمنا as the khabar.
His saying {من اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلا}: من is in the position of the genitive as a badal from النَّاس, and it is a badal of part from whole. Al-Kisāʾī allowed من to be conditional, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with استطاع in the position of the jussive by من, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) omitted, its implied form being "then upon him is the Hajj"; what indicates that is His saying وَمن كفر فَأن الله…, which is a condition without disagreement, and the first is like it. According to the Basrans it (وَمن كفر) is cut off from the first, a conditional mubtadaʾ. The hāʾ in إِلَيْهِ refers back to the House; and it was said to the Hajj.

mekki-muskil:99-99.t: His saying {وَأَنْتُم شُهَدَاء}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تَبْغُونَهَا.

mekki-muskil:101-101.t: His saying {وَأَنْتُم تتلى عَلَيْكُم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تكفرون; and likewise وَفِيكُمْ رَسُوله.

mekki-muskil:102-102.t:
His saying {تُقَاته}: its origin is وقية, and its explanation has preceded under تقاه [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. تقاة in verse 28].
His saying {وَأَنْتُم مُسلمُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تموتن, i.e. keep to this state until death comes to you while you are upon it.

mekki-muskil:103-103.t: His saying {جَمِيعًا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial); and إخوانا is the khabar (predicate) of أصبح.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t: His saying {إِلَّا أَذَى}: an exception not of the first kind (i.e. disjoined), in the position of the accusative.

mekki-muskil:113-113.t:
His saying {لَيْسُوا سَوَاء}: the noun (ism) of لَيْسَ is in it (the pronoun), and سَوَاء is its khabar (predicate), i.e. the believers and the transgressors mentioned before are not equal.
His saying {من أهل الْكتاب} أمة: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. Al-Farrāʾ allowed أمة to be nominative by سَوَاء, so that nothing from its khabar would refer back to the noun of لَيْسَ; this is not permissible, besides the ugliness of سَوَاء governing, since it does not run on the verb (i.e. is not verb-like); and moreover he implies in لَيْسَ what is not needed, since mention of the disbelievers has preceded. Abū ʿUbayda said أمة is the noun of لَيْسَ and سَوَاء is its khabar, and the pronoun in لَيْسَ came according to the dialect of those who say "the fleas ate me (أكلوني البراغيث)"; this is far-fetched, because those mentioned have come before لَيْسَ, whereas in أكلوني nothing has preceded, so this is not like it.
His saying {يَتلون آيَات الله}: in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أمة; and likewise وهم يَسْجُدُونَ: the position of the sentence is nominative as a naʿt of أمة. If you wish, you may put its position in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قَائِمَة, or from أمة when you make it nominative by سَوَاء; it would be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because recitation does not take place in prostration nor in bowing. The best in that is for it to be a clause with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: i.e. a ḥāl from أمة is permissible] because when an indefinite noun is strengthened by a naʿt it comes close to the definite, so a ḥāl from it is good, as He said وَهَذَا كتاب مُصدق لِسَانا عَرَبيا.
His saying {آنَاء اللَّيْل}: accusative as a ẓarf (adverb); it is an adverb of time meaning its hours. Its singular is إِنِّي, and it was said إِنِّي, and it was said أَنِّي [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended singulars are presumably إِنْي, إِنًى and أَنًى].

mekki-muskil:114-114.t: His saying {يُؤمنُونَ}: also in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of أمة; or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يَسْجُدُونَ, or from the pronoun in يَتلون, or from the pronoun in قَائِمَة — and the meaning of قَائِمَة is "upright". Likewise ويأمرون, وَينْهَوْنَ and ويسارعون. It is also permissible for all of that to be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

mekki-muskil:117-117.t:
His saying {فِيهَا صر}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ريح; and likewise أَصَابَت حرث قوم.
His saying {ظلمُوا أنفسهم}: the sentence is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of قوم.

mekki-muskil:118-118.t:
His saying {خبالا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification).
His saying {لَا يألونكم خبالا}: in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of بطانة; and likewise ودوا مَا عنتم. It is not good for ودوا to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) except with an implied قد, because it is a past verb.

mekki-muskil:119-119.t:
His saying {هَا أَنْتُم}: the hāʾ may be a replacement of a hamza, and it may be the هَا of drawing attention (tanbīh) — except in the reading of Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr, هأنتم with a hamza with fatḥa after the hāʾ, where it can only be a replacement of a hamza.
His saying {تحبونهم}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the vague noun (the demonstrative), or its ṣila (relative clause) if you make it in the sense of الَّذِي; it is like the one in al-Baqara, ثمَّ أَنْتُم هَؤُلَاءِ, and it has been explained.
His saying {وتؤمنون}: conjoined to تحبونهم.

mekki-muskil:120-120.t:
His saying {لَا يضركم}: whoever reads it with doubling and ḍamma (on the rāʾ) [Translator's note: the source reads «وَضم الْوَاو», evidently for «الرَّاء»], it may be jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition; but when he needed to vowel the doubled letter, he vowelled it with ḍamma and made it follow the ḍamma of what precedes it, as was said لم يردُّها with ḍamma. It was said it is nominative on an implied fāʾ; and it was said it is nominative with the intention of placing it before وَأَن تصبروا, as (the poet) said:
... إِنَّك إِن يصرع أَخُوك تصرع ...
(Indeed you, if your brother is thrown down, are thrown down.)
He put تصرع in the nominative with the intention of placing it first. The first is the best of them, although there is some difficulty in it. It is reported from ʿĀṣim that he read it with fatḥa on the doubled rāʾ, and that is better than the ḍamma. Whoever reads it light (without doubling) puts the rāʾ in the jussive because it is the apodosis of the condition; it is from ضاره يضيره, and al-Kisāʾī reported يضوره, so the ḍamma of the ḍād must be permissible.

mekki-muskil:121-121.t: His saying {وَإِذ غَدَوْت}: إِذْ is in the position of the accusative by an implied "remember (اذكر)". And His saying تبوىء الْمُؤمنِينَ is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ in غَدَوْت.

mekki-muskil:122-122.t: His saying {إِذْ هَمت}: إِذْ is in the position of the accusative, and what governs it is سميع عليم; it was said what governs it is تبوىء; and the first is better.

mekki-muskil:123-123.t: His saying {وَأَنْتُم أَذِلَّة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in يضركم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has نَصَرَكُمُ].

mekki-muskil:124-124.t:
His saying {إِذْ تَقول}: what governs إِذْ is يضركم [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably نَصَرَكُمُ of the previous verse].
His saying {أَن يمدكم}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of يكفي; its implied form is "will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforces you with three thousand?".
His saying {منزلين}: a naʿt (adjective) of ثَلَاثَة, and مسومين is a naʿt of خمسة. His saying وَمَا جعله الله: the hāʾ refers back to the reinforcing (al-imdād), indicated by يمددكم. It was said it refers back to the reinforcement (al-madad), who are the angels. It was said it refers back to the marking (al-taswīm), indicated by مسومين — and taswīm is taʿlīm (marking), i.e. marked, whom you recognize by the mark. It was said it refers back to the sending down, indicated by منزلين. And it was said it refers back to the number, indicated by "five thousand" — the thousand — and "three thousand", and that is a number.

mekki-muskil:127-127.t:
His saying {ليقطع طرفا}: the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a verb indicated by the speech, its implied form being "that He might cut off a portion, يضركم" [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «نصركم», "He gave you victory"]. It is also permissible for it to be attached to يمدكم.
His saying {أَو يكبتهم}: its origin according to many scholars is يكبدهم; then the dāl was replaced by tāʾ, as they said هرت الثَّوْب and هرده when he tore it. So it is taken from "Allah struck his liver (كبده) with evil, grief or rage".

mekki-muskil:128-128.t: His saying {أَو يَتُوب عَلَيْهِم أَو يعذبهم}: this is conjoined to ليقطع, and in the speech there is fronting and postponing. It was said it is accusative by an implied أَن, its meaning being "or that He turn (to them)" or "that He punish them".

mekki-muskil:130-130.t: His saying {أضعافا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl; and مضاعفة is its naʿt (adjective).

mekki-muskil:133-133.t: His saying {عرضهَا السَّمَاوَات وَالْأَرْض}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جنة; and likewise أعدت لِلْمُتقين.

mekki-muskil:136-136.t:
His saying {تجْرِي من تحتهَا}: تجْرِي is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
His saying {خَالِدين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أُولَئِكَ.

mekki-muskil:140-140.t:
His saying {قرح}: whoever reads it with ḍamma means the pain of wounds, and whoever reads it with fatḥa means the wound itself; and it was said they are two dialectal forms meaning wounds.
His saying {نداولها}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَيَّام.
Mujāhid read {من قبل أَن تلقوهُ} with ḍamma on the lām of قبل, making it a limit (ghāya, i.e. cut off from annexation); so the position of أَن is the accusative as a badal (substitute) from الْمَوْت, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). Whoever gives kasra to the lām of قبل, the position of أَن is the genitive by the annexation of قبل to it. The hāʾ in تلقوهُ refers back to death, and likewise the one in رَأَيْتُمُوهُ. By death here is meant meeting the enemy, because it is one of the causes of death, while the reality of death itself is not seen.

mekki-muskil:142-142.t: His saying {وَيعلم}: accusative by an implied أَن.

mekki-muskil:145-145.t:
His saying {وَمَا كَانَ لنَفس أَن تَمُوت}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of كَانَ; إِلَّا بإذن الله is the khabar (predicate), and لنفس is a fronted clarification (tabyīn).
His saying {كتابا مُؤَجّلا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:146-146.t:
His saying {وكأين}: it is أي upon which the kāf of comparison has entered, so the expression came to be in the sense of كم. A nūn is established in the muṣḥafs after the yāʾ, because it is a word transferred from its origin; so pausing on it is with the nūn, following the muṣḥaf. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr that he paused on it without nūn, according to the origin, because it is tanwīn.
As for whoever puts the hamza after (the alif) and makes it like فاعل (كائن), namely Ibn Kathīr: it was said that it is the active participle (fāʿil) from الكون (being); that is far-fetched because of من coming after it and because of its being indeclinable on sukūn. And it was said that it is the kāf of comparison that entered upon أي, and its use in the sense of كم became frequent so that it became a single word; then the yāʾ was moved before the hamza and it became كيء; then the doubled letter was lightened, as they lightened ميت and هين, so كيء became like فيعل; then they replaced the quiescent yāʾ with alif, as they replaced it in آيَة, whose origin is أأيية [Translator's note: so in the source]; so it became كأين. The origin of the nūn is tanwīn, so the analogy is to drop it in pause; but whoever pauses with the nūn argues that the word has been changed and metathesized, so the tanwīn became a letter of the root. Some of the Basrans said the origin in this reading is وكأي; then one of the two yāʾs was moved forward into the place of the hamza and was vowelled with fatḥa as the hamza had been, and the hamza became quiescent in the place of the yāʾ that had been moved forward; when the yāʾ was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa, it was turned into alif; the alif was quiescent with a quiescent hamza after it, so the hamza was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and one of the two yāʾs remained at the end, so the tanwīn removed it after the loss of its vowel, out of finding it heavy, as the yāʾ of قاض and غاز is dropped; so it became كاء, like جاء, the active participle of جاء. This view is reported from al-Khalīl.
His saying {مَعَه ربيون}: in the position of the genitive as a description of نبي, when you attribute the killing to the prophet and make it a description of him; ربيون on this (view) is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the ẓarf (adverbial phrase) — and that is better, because the ẓarf is a description of what precedes it, so it has the sense of a verb, and the nominative by it is strengthened. The nominative by the istiqrār (implied verb of settling) is weak only when the ẓarf does not rest on something before it, as in your saying فِي الدَّار زيد; but if you said مَرَرْت بِرَجُل فِي الدَّار أَبوهُ, the nominative of الأب by the istiqrār is good, because the ẓarf rests on what precedes it, so the sense of the verb becomes clear in it. The verb is more entitled to govern than the ibtidāʾ (being the subject), because the verb is a verbal (lafẓī) governor and the ibtidāʾ is an abstract (maʿnawī) governor, and the verbal is stronger than the abstract. So understand it, so that the meaning of the verse becomes clear to you. The hāʾ in مَعَه refers back to نبي.
It is also permissible to make مَعَه ربيون in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from نبي or from the pronoun in قتل, and the hāʾ in مَعَه would refer back to the pronoun in قتل. In both aspects مَعَه is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted in whose place it stands, and in it there is a reference (pronoun) from the omitted one, as though you said "settled with him are ربيون". If you attribute the verb to ربيون, they are nominative by قتل, and مَعَه becomes attached to قتل; so قتل and what follows it become a description of نبي. In the first aspect they were both descriptions of it, or قتل is a description and مَعَه ربيون is a ḥāl from نبي or from the pronoun in قتل, and that is better.
As for the khabar (predicate) of كأين: if you attribute قتل to نبي, you make مَعَه ربيون the khabar; or, if you wish, you make it a description of نبي, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in قتل or from نبي — because you have described it, as we mentioned — and imply the khabar, its implied form being "and how many a prophet has passed", or "has been in the world", and the like. If you attribute قتل to the ربيين, you make قتل مَعَه ربيون the khabar; or, if you wish, you make it a description of نبي and imply the khabar as before. Likewise is the implied form of this verse in the reading of whoever reads قَاتل: the matter is the same in both.
كأين is in the sense of كم, and there is no sense of comparison in the kāf in this, though that is its origin; but it has been changed from it and made, together with أي, a single word indicating what كم indicates in the declarative (khabar) use. So in the loss of the sense of comparison from it, it is like your saying "he has such-and-such (لَهُ كَذَا وَكَذَا)": the origin of the kāf is comparison, but it was made together with ذَا a single word, so the sense of comparison left it.
Al-Farrāʾ allowed {بل الله مولاكم} in the accusative, in the sense of "nay, obey Allah".

mekki-muskil:151-151.t: His saying {مَا لم ينزل}: مَا is the object of أشركوا.

mekki-muskil:154-154.t:
His saying {أَمَنَة نعاسا}: (أمنة is) the object of أنزل, and نعاسا is a badal (substitute) from أمنة. It was said أمنة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) and نعاس is accusative by أنزل.
His saying {وَطَائِفَة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is قد أهمتهم, and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). This wāw: it was said it is the wāw of ibtidāʾ (beginning), it was said it is the wāw of the ḥāl, and it was said it is in the sense of إِذْ.
His saying {يظنون} {وَيَقُولُونَ}: both are in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of طائفة, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in أهمتهم.
His saying {كُله لله}: whoever reads it in the accusative makes it a tawkīd (emphasis) of الأمر, and لله is the khabar of إن; al-Akhfash said it is a badal from الأمر. Whoever reads it in the nominative does so as mubtadaʾ, with لله its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of إن.
His saying {وليبتلي الله مَا فِي صدوركم}: the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a verb indicated by the speech, its implied form being "and so that Allah might test what is in your breasts, He prescribed fighting for you". And وليمحص is conjoined to وليبتلي.

mekki-muskil:159-159.t: His saying {فبمَا رَحْمَة من الله}: رَحْمَة is genitive by the bāʾ, and مَا is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. Ibn Kaysān said مَا is an indefinite noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and رَحْمَة is a badal (substitute) from مَا or a naʿt (adjective) of it. The nominative of رَحْمَة is also permissible, on the basis that you make مَا in the sense of الَّذِي and imply هُوَ in the ṣila (relative clause) and drop it, as was read تَمامًا على الَّذِي أحسنُ. The hāʾ in من بعده refers back to Allah, exalted be His mention; and it was said it refers back to the forsaking (al-khidhlān).

mekki-muskil:161-161.t: His saying {أَن يغل}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of كَانَ. Whoever reads أَن يَغُلّ with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the ghayn, its meaning is "it is not for a prophet to betray anyone in booty or anything else". Whoever reads it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ghayn (يُغَلّ), its meaning is "it is not for a prophet to be found a betrayer", as you say أحمدت الرجل, "I found him praiseworthy", and أحمقته, "I found him foolish". And it was said its meaning is "it is not for a prophet to be betrayed, or that his companions betray him, in booty or anything else".

mekki-muskil:168-168.t: His saying {الَّذين قَالُوا لإخوانهم}: الَّذين is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of الَّذين نافقوا, or as a badal (substitute), or by an implied أَعنِي ("I mean"); or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:170-170.t:
His saying {فرحين}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يرْزقُونَ. If it were in ordinary speech, فَرِحُونَ would be permissible as a naʿt (adjective) of أحياء.
His saying {أَلا خوف}: أَن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from الَّذين, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). It is also permissible for it to be in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "in that not (بِأَن لَا)".

mekki-muskil:172-172.t: His saying {الَّذين اسْتَجَابُوا}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) comes after مَا أَصَابَهُم الْقرح. It is also permissible for الَّذين to be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from الْمُؤمنِينَ, or from الَّذين لم يلْحقُوا بهم.

mekki-muskil:173-173.t: His saying {الَّذين قَالَ لَهُم النَّاس}: a badal (substitute) from الَّذين اسْتَجَابُوا.

mekki-muskil:178-178.t:
His saying {وَلَا يَحسبن الَّذين كفرُوا أَنما نملي لَهُم}: أن takes the place of the two objects of حسب, and الَّذين is the agents (fāʿil). مَا in أنما is in the sense of الَّذِي, and the hāʾ is omitted from نملي. This is according to the reading of whoever reads it with bāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently «بالياء», with yāʾ]; and خير is the khabar (predicate) of أن. If you wish, you may make مَا with نملي a maṣdar (verbal noun), so you do not imply a hāʾ; its implied form is "and let not those who disbelieve think that the respite is better for them". As for whoever reads with yāʾ and gives kasra to the أن of إنما, that is permissible only on the basis that حسب is suspended (taʿlīq) and an oath is implied, as you do with the lām of ibtidāʾ in your saying لَا يَحسبن زيد لأخوه أفضل من عَمْرو, as though you said "by Allah, his brother is better than ʿAmr".
As for whoever reads it with tāʾ, namely Ḥamza, he makes الَّذين the first object of تحسبن, and the agent is the one addressed, namely the Prophet, upon him be peace; and he makes أنما and what follows it a badal (substitute) from الَّذين, so it stands in place of the two objects, as has passed in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ; مَا in this reading is in the sense of الَّذِي, and the hāʾ is omitted from نملي. It is not good to make أن a second object of حسب, because the second in this chapter is the first in meaning — unless you imply something omitted, its implied form being "and do not think the affair of those who disbelieve is that We grant them respite", making مَا with نملي a maṣdar on this (view). If you do not imply something omitted, its permissibility rests on أن being a badal from الَّذين and standing in place of the two objects, with مَا in the sense of الَّذِي; and there is room for reflection regarding the permissibility of مَا with the verb being a maṣdar and أن being a badal from الَّذين. It would have been a valid way of reading, for whoever reads with tāʾ, to give kasra to إنما, so that the sentence would be in the position of the second object; but no one that I know of read it so. It has been said that the permissibility (of the reading) of whoever reads with tāʾ is by way of repetition (takrīr), its implied form being "do not think those who disbelieve — and do not think that We grant them respite…", so إنما stands in place of the two objects of the second تحسب, and it, together with what it governs, is the second object of the first تحسب; just as if you said الَّذين كفرُوا لَا تحسبن إِنَّمَا نملي لَهُم خير لأَنْفُسِهِمْ it would be permissible, and the first تحسب enters upon the mubtadaʾ (subject).
